_comment: Committed persistence declaration per module (a decision, not a measurement); read by tools/cardmeta_footprint.py, which adds sizes and counts from the live state. Paths: repo-relative, absolute or ~/...; <project> is replaced by the project name; kind 'dir' counts files. 'volume': true marks files whose modification times feed the volume figures. A missing backup or retention statement is a gap and is shown as such: gaps below are honest 'undocumented' entries, not decisions. Backup 'undocumented' means nobody has decided yet (the cockpit shows it as a gap); the code itself is in git.

files.note: access token of the service (mode 0600); a secret, not personal data; one token serves all projects of one Cockpit instance, so it lives in the folder of the project named in the service's --token-file, not in every project's folder: a project whose folder has none shows it as not present

standard output and error of the launchd job (the cockpit logger writes to standard error); the request log hides the token; only in the folder named in the job's log settings; never rotated (a gap, see the policy)
the Dispatcher's settings, written by the Settings page (mode 0600, atomically); an owner decision, read by taskqueue/dispatcher at each firing; a missing file means the defaults
module-card options of the Settings tab (churn colour and the quality-band thresholds; mode 0600, written atomically); an owner decision; a missing file means the defaults
the list of projects the Cockpit serves (the --projects file); written by hand, only read by githubclient

read only, by get_usage for the Token Usage page (a missing file shows as no data) and by tools/token_reconcile.py (the card How these numbers fit); exact token counts of interactive and (earlier) headless sessions, each record with its kind, numbers and ids only

read only, by get_usage for the Token Usage page (a missing file shows as no data) and by tools/token_reconcile.py; daily token totals per model and daily message and session counts from the vendor tool's statistics cache, a coarse backfill marked source stats-cache; numbers only; rewritten whole on each run, rebuildable while the cache exists

not ours: read only, when the projects file names it (key stats_cache) or tools/token_reconcile.py gets --cache, for the card How these numbers fit; only its daily numbers are read, nothing is copied or written. tools/token_reconcile.py writes no file: it reads the quota, proxy, transcript, backfill and processing files and the good-bye notes of the data folder and prints its report

disk copies of the state, rules, timeline, card data, code view and module-page inputs (JSON, the --cache-dir argument); shown at once after a restart (a copy younger than one hour is not refreshed at all, so a restart costs no GitHub call) and refreshed behind; holds GitHub issue data (titles, bodies, labels), no token; rebuildable

logging.rotation: none recorded: the logger writes to standard error, which the launchd job appends to cockpit.log without rotation (about 2.8 MB after three days); the request log hides the token

policy.backup: code: the git repository and its remote; the settings files (dispatcher-settings.json, cockpit-settings.json) and projects.json are owner decisions, not rebuildable: they and the project's files of the cache folder go into the daily backup to Drive (PC-62, tools/project_backup.py; so that a copy of the Cockpit can run from the backup alone); the token file is a secret and is never backed up; the log and the in-memory cache are not backed up on purpose
policy.retention: in-memory cache: lives with the process, entries refresh after 60 to 3600 seconds (GitHub-sourced data after 3600 s) (cached() in cockpit.py); token file: kept until the owner deletes it, no rotation in the code; cockpit.log: grows without limit (no rotation yet: open); settings files: kept; no database; cache folder: files are overwritten on each refresh and never pruned, safe to delete at any time

policy.backup: the page: the git repository and its remote; browser storage is not backed up on purpose
policy.retention: browser localStorage only, never sent anywhere: key cockpit-project (selected project) and cockpit-reviewed:<repo> (review state of rule changes); kept until the user clears site data

policy.backup: the git repository and its remote; nothing else to back up
policy.retention: kept until the owner deletes them (git history)

files.note: 6a: interval, on/off switch, retries, number of Workers and the three limits; outside git; read at each firing (6b); the path is a suggested default, the code takes it as an argument
the Workers a firing leaves running for the next one (3o)
4q: one folder per task with inbox/ (main.bundle, task.md) and outbox/ (started, goodbye.json, result.bundle); task text comes from issues, so check before sharing
4h: token usage per Worker, one JSON line per request; counts only
the vendor's quota percentages over time, one JSON line per change (every 30 seconds at most); append-only, kept, backed up; percentages and reset times only

the exact token counts of the owner's interactive sessions and of the earlier headless Worker sessions, one JSON line per message (time, kind, source label, session id, message id, model, four counts); mode 0600; numbers only, no text or paths; rewritten atomically on each run; in the daily backup (PC-62)
4f: the host Unix socket the proxy listens on (path under 104 bytes); a socket, no content

5a-5d: the processing log, one JSON line per entry naming task and task folder; on the owner's MacBook, outside any git repository; the daily backup access details live in a configuration file outside git
5e: the date of the last daily backup of the processing log; a date only

files.written_by: launchd (the Dispatcher's standard output and error)
files.note: 3c: what the Dispatcher's loggers write at each firing (path set in dispatcher/launchd.py)

files.written_by: launchd (the quota collector's standard output and error)
files.note: the quota collector's log, one reading every 30 seconds (path set in dispatcher/launchd.py)
the two rendered LaunchAgent files (Dispatcher, quota collector); they hold the token-file path, not the token
SENSITIVE: the owner's subscription credential the proxy adds to requests (4g); outside git, never logged or printed; the path is a suggested default, the code takes it as an argument

logging.file: dispatcher.log (standard output and error under launchd); the processing log (processing/processing.jsonl) holds the entries of 5a, 5b
logging.rotation: none in the code; the processing log is backed up once a day
none: one summary line per run on standard error (sources, files, messages, skipped); no message text is ever logged
none: the proxy is started detached with its output discarded (start_proxy), so it keeps no log file; usage goes to proxy-usage.jsonl; the token is never logged

policy.backup: code: the git repository and its remote; the processing log: once a day to GDrive (5e); the daily backup of the project's Cockpit data (PC-62, tools/project_backup.py) holds the processing log, settings, state, proxy usage, quota history, transcript usage and the Workers' good-bye notes; logs, rendered LaunchAgent files, the socket and the task bundles (code) are not backed up on purpose; the token files are secrets and are never backed up
policy.retention: processing log: kept, no rotation in the code; task folders: not torn down by the Dispatcher, old ones are mopped up later (3m); settings, state and token: kept until the owner changes or deletes them; transcript-usage.jsonl: rewritten on each run; no database tables

files.note: the Workers' image sources (Containerfile, Stop hook, skill); the built image and the container's own disk are held by the container tool, where the clones of the tasks live (4l)

logging.rotation: none: the relay runs inside the container and writes to its standard error
none: the Stop hook runs inside the container and writes warnings to its standard error

policy.backup: the image sources: the git repository and its remote; the built image and the clones on the container's own disk are rebuildable or fetched back as bundles and are not backed up on purpose
policy.retention: the image is kept until rebuilt; clones live on the container's own disk until the container is removed (the Dispatcher does not tear them down, 3m)

files.note: scratch folder of one failure-path run: the throwaway repository's clone, the Dispatcher's state and processing log of that run; created by the driver and not kept on purpose
the model stub and the Containerfile of the derived stub image (sources only); the built image is held by the container tool

logging.rotation: none: the driver writes to its standard error
none: the stub runs inside the container and writes to its standard error

policy.backup: the driver and the stub: the git repository and its remote; the scratch folder and the stub image are rebuildable and are not backed up on purpose
policy.retention: the scratch folder is the caller's to delete (a run does not clean the folder it was given); the stub image is kept until rebuilt

files.note: screenshots made by tools/shots.py; they show whatever the cockpit showed, so check before publishing

policy.backup: the git repository and its remote; nothing else to back up
policy.retention: kept until the owner deletes them (git history)

policy.retention: kept until the owner deletes them (git history)

files.note: the last compliance report of the project's local policy files (date, constitution version, violations, semantic candidates when that layer ran); replaced on every run; read by the Cockpit page

the status record of the last daily backup (time, ok, archive path, size, number of files, reason, last good time); replaced atomically after every run; read by the gap checker (kind backup) and the Task Queue tab

SENSITIVE: the mirror of the coding tool's raw session transcripts of the project (owner, 2026-11-24): conversation text, may hold secrets or personal data; new and grown files are copied, nothing is ever deleted (the tool deletes old ones); goes only into the owner's own Drive

one dated archive a day (<project>-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz, a taken name gets -2, -3, ...), written create-only into the folder the Drive desktop app syncs; holds the transcripts, so personal data; never edited or deleted by the job

logging.rotation: none: one line per step on standard error, kept by whatever runs the daily job; never logs file contents

policy.backup: the job and the retention script: the git repository and its remote; the status record and the transcript mirror are themselves in each daily archive; the archives in Drive are the backup
policy.retention: archives in Drive: the newest 30 per project, kept by the Apps Script tools/drive_retention.gs that the owner installs (a count, not an age: a pause in the backups removes nothing); transcript mirror: never pruned; status record: replaced at each run

policy.backup: the git repository and its remote; nothing else to back up
policy.retention: kept until the owner deletes them (git history)

files.note: footprint.json, churn.json, ambiguity.json: generated, overwritten at each run, never committed; names, counts and sizes only
the last code snapshot refresh of the daily job (time, action, exit code, reason, snapshot age); replaced at every run, never committed; the collector's output goes to the log, not into this file

logging.rotation: none: the collectors write to standard error, no log file

policy.backup: map and collectors: the git repository and its remote; the generated card data is in the daily backup of the project's Cockpit data (PC-62), so that an offline copy shows the cards
policy.retention: only the latest run is kept (files are replaced); no history
